verbalization: Oblonganoside C appears to exert its biological effects through a multi-tiered mechanism involving the glutamine--fructose-6-phosphate aminotransferase [isomerizing] enzyme. The evidence suggests that this compound targets two distinct entities: Serine/threonine-protein kinase SBK1, which in turn is targeted by benzocaine, and Caov-4, which is targeted by K-252a. Both benzocaine and K-252a are known to modulate the activity of the glutamine--fructose-6-phosphate aminotransferase [isomerizing] enzyme, indicating a potential pathway through which Oblonganoside C may influence this target. The final scores from the two paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of two distinct targets and their shared downstream effect on the enzyme underscores the complexity of the pathway, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct involvement of Oblonganoside C in regulating this specific enzyme.
